title.zh: 卷四百九十一 列傳第二百五十 外國七 流求國 定安國 渤海國 日本國 党項
title.en: Volume 491 Biographies 250: Foreign States 7: Ryukyu Islands, Ding'an, Bohai, Japan, Tangut
title.raw: 卷四百九十一 列傳第二百五十 外國七 流求國 定安國 渤海國 日本國 党項 Volume 491 Biographies 250: Foreign States 7: Ryukyu Islands, Ding'an, Bohai, Japan, Tangut

sentences.zh: 流求國 定安國 渤海國 日本國 党項

translations.literal: The State of Ryukyu, the State of Ding'an, the State of Bohai, the State of Japan, and the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: Ryukyu, Ding'an, Bohai, Japan, and the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 流求國

translations.literal: The State of Ryukyu.
translations.idiomatic: Ryukyu

sentences.zh: 流求國在泉州之東，有海島曰彭湖，煙火相望。

translations.literal: The State of Ryukyu lies east of Quanzhou; there is a sea island called Penghu, and their fires and smoke are visible to each other across the water.
translations.idiomatic: Ryukyu lay east of Quanzhou; an offshore island called Penghu stood between them, close enough that hearth fires were visible from shore to shore.

sentences.zh: 其國塹柵三重，環以流水，植棘爲藩，以刀槊弓矢劍鈹爲兵器，視月盈虧以紀時。

translations.literal: Their state had triple moats and palisades, encircled by flowing water; they planted thorns as fences, used knives, spears, bows, arrows, swords, and halberds as weapons, and reckoned time by the waxing and waning of the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Their settlements were ringed by three lines of ditch and palisade with running water between them, thorn hedges for walls, and arms of blade, spear, bow, arrow, sword, and halberd; they kept time by the phases of the moon.

sentences.zh: 無他奇貨，商賈不通，厥土沃壤，無賦斂，有事則均稅。

translations.literal: They had no other rare goods; merchants did not come and go. Their soil was fertile; there were no regular levies—when there was business, taxes were assessed equally.
translations.idiomatic: They produced no exotic trade goods and had little commerce with merchants. The land was rich, with no standing tax; when the community needed funds, everyone paid an equal share.

sentences.zh: 旁有毗舍邪國，語言不通，袒裸盱睢，殆非人類。

translations.literal: Nearby was the state of Piseye; languages did not communicate; they went naked with staring eyes—hardly human.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby lived the people of Piseye, with whom they could not speak; they went about naked and wide-eyed, seeming scarcely human at all.

sentences.zh: 淳熙間，國之酋豪嘗率數百輩猝至泉之水沃、圍頭等村，肆行殺掠。

translations.literal: During the Chunxi era, the chieftains of the state once led several hundred men in a sudden descent on the villages of Shuiwo and Weitou in Quanzhou, killing and plundering at will.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chunxi period, Ryukyu chiefs once led several hundred warriors in a surprise raid on Quanzhou villages such as Shuiwo and Weitou, killing and looting freely.

sentences.zh: 喜鐵器及匙箸，人閉戶則免，但刓其門圈而去。

translations.literal: They delighted in iron objects and spoons and chopsticks; if people closed their doors they were spared, but the door rings were gouged out and taken away.
translations.idiomatic: They coveted iron and household utensils; households that barred their doors were usually left alone, but the metal door fittings were pried out and carried off.

sentences.zh: 擲以匙箸則頫拾之，見鐵騎則爭剚其甲，駢首就戮而不知悔。

translations.literal: If spoons and chopsticks were thrown to them they would bow and pick them up; when they saw armored horsemen they would vie to stab through the armor, dying head to head without knowing regret.
translations.idiomatic: Thrown spoons or chopsticks, they would stoop to snatch them up; at the sight of armored cavalry they fought to pierce the mail, falling in heaps without a thought of retreat.

sentences.zh: 臨敵用標槍，繫繩十餘丈爲操縱，蓋惜其鐵不忍棄也。

translations.literal: In battle they used throwing spears, with ropes of more than ten zhang for control—because they cherished their iron and could not bear to abandon it.
translations.idiomatic: In combat they used javelins on cords more than ten zhang long so they could recover the heads—iron was too precious to leave behind.

sentences.zh: 不駕舟楫，惟縛竹爲筏，急則群舁之泅水而遁。

translations.literal: They did not use boats; they only bound bamboo into rafts, and in urgency the group would lift them and swim away.
translations.idiomatic: They did not sail proper boats, only lashed bamboo rafts; in a pinch they would shoulder the rafts and swim away together.

sentences.zh: 定安國

translations.literal: The State of Ding'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ding'an

sentences.zh: 定安國本馬韓之種，爲契丹所攻破，其酋帥糾合餘衆，保於西鄙，建國改元，自稱定安國。

translations.literal: The State of Ding'an was originally of the Mahan stock; it was broken by the Khitan. Its chieftain gathered the remaining people, held the western marches, established a state and changed the era name, and styled himself the State of Ding'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ding'an sprang from the Mahan people. After the Khitan overran them, a chief rallied the survivors on the western frontier, founded a kingdom with its own reign title, and called it Ding'an.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，其國王烈萬華因女真遣使入貢，乃附表貢獻方物。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao, its king Liewanhua, because the Jurchen sent envoys to offer tribute, attached a memorial and presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 3 (970), King Liewanhua sent a memorial and tribute goods along with a Jurchen embassy bound for the Song court.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，太宗方經營遠略，討擊契丹，因降詔其國，令張犄角之勢。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo, Emperor Taizong was pursuing far-reaching strategy and attacking the Khitan; he therefore issued an edict to their state ordering them to spread a pincer posture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiping Xingguo era, as Taizong pressed his northern campaign against the Khitan, he sent Ding'an an edict instructing it to threaten the enemy from the flank.

sentences.zh: 其國亦怨寇仇侵侮不已，聞中國用兵北討，欲依王師以攄宿憤，得詔大喜。

translations.literal: Their state also resented that the enemy had ceaselessly invaded and insulted them; hearing that China was using troops to campaign north, they wished to rely on the imperial army to vent long-held anger, and upon receiving the edict were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Ding'an too had long smarted under Khitan raids; when word came that the Song were marching north, they hoped to march with the imperial host and settle old scores, and they rejoiced at the edict.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，會女真遣使來貢，路由本國，乃托其使附表來上云：「定安國王臣烏玄明言：伏遇聖主洽天地之恩，撫夷貊之俗，臣玄明誠喜誠抃，頓首頓首。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year, when the Jurchen sent envoys to offer tribute and their route passed through this state, he entrusted their envoy to attach a memorial and present it, saying: 'The King of Ding'an, your subject Wuxuanming, speaks: I have encountered the sage lord who harmonizes the grace of Heaven and Earth and cherishes the customs of the Yi and Mo; your subject Xuanming is truly joyful and truly exultant—bowing head, bowing head.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year six, a Jurchen tribute mission passed through Ding'an; the king entrusted them with a memorial that read: 'King Wuxuanming of Ding'an reports: Having met a sage emperor who joins Heaven and Earth in grace and nurtures the border peoples, I am filled with joy—your servant bows again and again.

sentences.zh: 臣本以高麗舊壤，渤海遺黎，保據方隅，涉曆星紀，仰覆露鴻鈞之德，被浸漬無外之澤，各得其所，以遂本性。

translations.literal: Your subject was originally on the old soil of Goryeo, the remnant people of Bohai, holding a corner of the realm through cycles of the stars; looking up to the virtue of the vast dome, soaked in the moisture of boundless favor, each has obtained his place to follow his nature.
translations.idiomatic: We are heirs of Goryeo's old domain and Bohai's scattered folk, holding a remote corner through many years. Under your all-embracing majesty and ceaseless favor, each of us has found a place to live as we are.

sentences.zh: 而頃歲契丹恃其強暴，入寇境土，攻破城砦，俘略人民。

translations.literal: But in recent years the Khitan, relying on their violence, entered and raided our territory, broke city walls and forts, and captured and carried off the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent years the Khitan, trusting in their brute force, have invaded our lands, stormed our fortresses, and carried off our people.

sentences.zh: 臣祖考守節不降，與衆避地，僅存生聚，以迄於今。

translations.literal: Your subject's grandfather and father held to integrity and did not submit; with the multitude they fled the land, barely preserving life and settlement down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: My forefathers refused to submit and led our people into exile; only a remnant community survives to this day.

sentences.zh: 而又扶餘府昨背契丹，並歸本國，災禍將至，無大於此。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Fuyu prefecture has now turned against the Khitan and all come back to our state—no calamity about to arrive is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Now Fuyu has broken with the Khitan and thrown in with us; no peril could be greater if we fail to act.

sentences.zh: 所宜受天朝之密畫，率勝兵而助討，必欲報敵，不敢違命。

translations.literal: It is fitting to receive the secret plan of the heavenly court, lead victorious troops to assist the punitive campaign, and be certain to repay the enemy—I dare not disobey the command.
translations.idiomatic: We should accept your secret design, march our best troops to aid the campaign, and repay the enemy without fail—your servant will not disobey.

sentences.zh: 臣玄明誠懇誠願，頓首頓首。」

translations.literal: Your subject Xuanming is truly earnest and truly willing—bowing head, bowing head.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Xuanming offers this in all sincerity—again I bow.'

sentences.zh: 其末題云：「元興六年十月日，定安國王臣玄明表上聖皇帝前。」

translations.literal: At the end it was inscribed: 'Sixth year of Yuanxing, tenth month, day—Memorial of the King of Ding'an, your subject Xuanming, presented before the Sage Emperor.'
translations.idiomatic: The colophon read: 'Tenth month, sixth year of Yuanxing—memorial of King Xuanming of Ding'an to the Sage Emperor.'

sentences.zh: 上答以詔書曰：「敕定安國王烏玄明。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with an edict, saying: 'Imperial command to the King of Ding'an, Wuxuanming.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with an edict: 'To King Wuxuanming of Ding'an.

sentences.zh: 女真使至，得所上表，以朕嘗賜手詔諭旨，且陳感激。

translations.literal: The Jurchen envoy arrived and we received your submitted memorial; you say that I once bestowed a handwritten edict of instruction, and moreover express gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Your memorial came with the Jurchen envoys; you recall the personal edict I once sent you and declare your gratitude.

sentences.zh: 卿遠國豪帥，名王茂緒，奄有馬韓之地，介於鯨海之表，強敵吞併，失其故土，沉冤未報，積憤奚伸。

translations.literal: You are a heroic leader of a distant state, a famous king of flourishing line, who broadly holds the land of Mahan between the whale seas; a strong enemy swallowed and merged you, you lost your old territory, deep grievance is unavenged—how can accumulated rage be released?
translations.idiomatic: You are a famed king of a distant realm, lord of Mahan's lands between the eastern seas; a powerful foe swallowed your country and drove you from your homeland, and long injustice still cries for vengeance.

sentences.zh: 矧彼獯戎，尚搖蠆毒，出師以薄伐，乘夫天災之流行，敗衄相尋，滅亡可待。

translations.literal: Moreover those northern barbarians still shake their poison; we shall send out the army for a pressing campaign, riding the spread of heavenly calamities—defeats will follow in succession, and extinction awaits.
translations.idiomatic: Those northern tribes still stir up trouble; we shall march against them and, as Heaven sends disaster upon them, defeat after defeat will bring their end near.

sentences.zh: 今國家已于邊郡廣屯重兵，只俟嚴冬，即申天討。

translations.literal: Now the state has already massed heavy troops widely in the border prefectures; we only await deep winter, then will execute Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The court has already massed great armies on the frontier and waits only for deep winter to launch Heaven's punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 卿若能追念累世之恥，宿戒舉國之師，當予伐罪之秋，展爾復仇之志，朔漠底定，爵賞有加，宜思永圖，無失良便。

translations.literal: If you can recall the shame of many generations, make long preparation and raise the army of the whole state, at the season when we punish crime you may display your will to take revenge; when the northern desert is settled, titles and rewards will be increased—you should think of a lasting plan and not miss the good opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: If you will remember generations of humiliation and ready your whole kingdom, then when we strike you may fulfill your wish for revenge; when the northern steppe is pacified, honors will be heaped upon you—plan for the long term and do not let this chance slip.

sentences.zh: 而況渤海願歸於朝化，扶余已背於賊庭，勵乃宿心，糾其協力，克期同舉，必集大勳。

translations.literal: Moreover Bohai wishes to return to the court's transformation; Fuyu has already turned from the rebel court—strengthen your long-held resolve, gather their joint strength, fix the day for a common rising, and great merit will surely be gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai yearns to submit to the court, and Fuyu has already broken with the Khitan; steel your old resolve, join forces with them, and strike on the appointed day—great merit awaits.

sentences.zh: 尚阻重溟，未遑遣使，倚注之切，鑒寐寧忘。」

translations.literal: Still blocked by the heavy seas, we have not yet been able to send envoys; our reliance and expectation are keen—in waking or sleeping how could we forget?'
translations.idiomatic: The wide seas still keep us from sending envoys in person, but our trust in you is deep, and we do not forget you waking or sleeping.'

sentences.zh: 以詔付女真使，令齎以賜之。

translations.literal: The edict was given to the Jurchen envoy and he was ordered to carry it as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was entrusted to the Jurchen envoys to deliver to him.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，其王子因女真使附獻馬、雕羽鳴鏑。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, its prince, through the Jurchen envoy, additionally presented horses and whistling arrows with carved feathers.
translations.idiomatic: In Duangong 2 (989), the crown prince sent horses and carved-feather whistling arrows by way of a Jurchen embassy.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，其五子太元因女真使上表，其後不復至。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, its fifth son Taiyuan submitted a memorial through the Jurchen envoy; after that they did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 2 (991), his fifth son Taiyuan sent a memorial through the Jurchen; no further embassies followed.

sentences.zh: 渤海國

translations.literal: The State of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai

sentences.zh: 渤海本高麗之別種。

translations.literal: Bohai was originally a separate branch of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai was originally a Goryeo offshoot.

sentences.zh: 唐高宗平高麗，徙其人居中國。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong of Tang pacified Goryeo and moved its people into China.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Gaozong conquered Goryeo, he resettled many of its people within the empire.

sentences.zh: 則天萬歲通天中，契丹攻陷營府，高麗別種大祚榮走保遼東，睿宗以爲忽汗州都督，封渤海郡王，因自稱渤海國，並有扶餘、肅慎等十餘國，歷唐、梁、後唐，朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era of Empress Zetian, the Khitan attacked and took Ying Prefecture; the Goryeo offshoot Dazu Rong fled to hold eastern Liaodong; Emperor Ruizong made him Grand Protector of Huhan Prefecture and enfeoffed him as Prince of Bohai Commandery, whereupon he styled himself the State of Bohai, and together held more than ten states including Fuyu and Sushen; through Tang, Liang, and Later Tang, tribute missions never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's Wansui Tongtian reign, the Khitan captured Ying Prefecture; the Goryeo chieftain Dazu Rong withdrew into eastern Liaodong. Ruizong appointed him Protector-General of Huhan and Prince of Bohai, and he proclaimed the kingdom of Bohai, absorbing Fuyu, Sushen, and more than a dozen other states. Through Tang, Later Liang, and Later Tang, Bohai tribute never lapsed.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成初，爲契丹阿保機攻扶餘城下之，改扶餘爲東丹府，命其子突欲留兵鎮之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng in Later Tang, Abaoji of the Khitan attacked and took Fuyu below its walls, changed Fuyu to the Eastern Dan Prefecture, and ordered his son Tuyu to remain with troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Later Tang Tiancheng (926–927), the Khitan ruler Abaoji stormed Fuyu, renamed it the Eastern Dan prefecture, and left his son Tuyu to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 阿保機死，渤海王復攻扶餘，不能克。

translations.literal: When Abaoji died, the King of Bohai again attacked Fuyu but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: After Abaoji's death the Bohai king attacked Fuyu again but failed to retake it.

sentences.zh: 歷長興、清泰，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Through Changxing and Qingtai, they sent envoys to offer court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Changxing and Qingtai reigns they continued to send tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，其酋豪崔烏斯等三十人來歸，其後隔絕不能通中國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande in Zhou, its chieftains Cui Wusi and thirty others came to submit; afterward they were cut off and could not reach China.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Later Zhou Xiande (954), thirty Bohai leaders including Cui Wusi defected to the court; afterward contact with China was lost.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，太宗平晉陽，移兵幽州，其酋帥大鸞河率小校李勳等十六人、部族三百騎來降，以鸞河爲渤海都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, Taizong pacified Jinyang and shifted troops to Youzhou; its chieftain Daluanhe led junior officers Li Xun and sixteen others and three hundred horsemen of the tribe to surrender, and Daluanhe was made Bohai Metropolitan Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4 (979), after Taizong took Jinyang and marched on Youzhou, the Bohai chief Daluanhe arrived with sixteen officers including Li Xun and three hundred tribesmen to surrender; Daluanhe was appointed metropolitan commander of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 六年，賜烏舍城浮渝府渤海琰府王詔曰：「朕纂紹丕構，奄有四海，普天之下，罔不率俾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict was bestowed on the King of the Bohai Yan Prefecture of the Fuyu Circuit of Wushe City, saying: 'I have succeeded to the great foundation and broadly possess the four seas; under all Heaven, none does not follow and submit.
translations.idiomatic: In year six the court sent an edict to the Bohai king of Wushe City's Fuyu circuit: 'Having inherited the great enterprise, I hold the four seas; all under Heaven now follow and submit.

sentences.zh: 矧太原封域，國之保障，頃因竊據，遂相承襲，倚限定爲援，歷世逋誅。

translations.literal: Moreover Taiyuan's sealed domain is the state's bulwark; recently because of usurped occupation it was passed down in succession, relying on Ding as a support, evading punishment through generations.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan is the empire's shield; for years rebels held it and passed it from hand to hand, using Ding as their patron and defying imperial justice generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 朕前歲親提銳旅，盡護諸將，拔並門之孤壘，斷匈奴之右臂，眷言吊伐，以蘇黔黎。

translations.literal: Last year I personally led sharp troops, fully protecting the generals, took the lone fortress of Bing Gate, cut off the right arm of the Xiongnu, lovingly speaking of punitive expedition to relieve the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: Last year I led the army in person, shielded every general, stormed the lone fortress at Bing Gate, and severed the barbarians' right arm—this campaign was waged to rescue the common people.

sentences.zh: 蠢茲北戎，非理構怨，輒肆薦食，犯我封略。

translations.literal: These foolish northern barbarians, without reason stirring resentment, then wildly spread like locusts eating and violated our borders.
translations.idiomatic: Those foolish northern tribes, nursing grievances without cause, have swarmed like locusts against our frontiers.

sentences.zh: 一昨出師逆擊，斬獲甚衆。

translations.literal: The day before yesterday we sent out the army to strike in counterattack, and beheaded and captured very many.
translations.idiomatic: In our recent counterattack we killed and captured a great host of them.

sentences.zh: 今欲鼓行深入，席捲長驅，焚其龍庭，大殲丑類。

translations.literal: Now we wish to beat the drums and advance deep, sweep forward in long drive, burn their dragon court, and greatly annihilate the ugly kind.
translations.idiomatic: Now we mean to march deep into their lands, sweep forward without pause, burn their royal encampment, and destroy their forces utterly.

sentences.zh: 素聞爾國密邇寇仇，迫於吞併，力不能制，因而服屬，困於率割。

translations.literal: We have long heard that your state lies close to the enemy, pressed by annexation, strength unable to control them, and thus submitted in subordination, trapped in repeated exactions.
translations.idiomatic: We have long known that your kingdom lies hard by the enemy, too weak to resist their swallowing you up, and so you submitted—only to suffer their endless levies.

sentences.zh: 當靈旗破敵之際，是鄰邦雪憤之日，所宜盡出族帳，佐予兵鋒。

translations.literal: When the spirit banners break the enemy, that is the day for neighboring states to vent their anger; you should fully bring out the clan tents to assist our military edge.
translations.idiomatic: When our banners break the foe, it will be your day to settle old scores; you should muster every clan and camp to fight at our side.

sentences.zh: 俟其翦滅，沛然封賞，幽、薊土宇，復歸中原，朔漠之外，悉以相與。

translations.literal: When they are cut down and extinguished, rewards and enfeoffments will pour forth; the lands of You and Ji will return to the Central Plains, and everything beyond the northern desert will all be given to you.
translations.idiomatic: Once they are destroyed, honors will flow in abundance; You and Ji will return to the heartland, and all lands beyond the northern desert shall be yours.

sentences.zh: 勖乃協力，朕不食言。」

translations.literal: Exhort yourselves to joint effort—I do not eat my words.'
translations.idiomatic: Exert yourselves in concert; I do not break my word.'

sentences.zh: 時將大舉征契丹，故降是詔諭旨。

translations.literal: At that time a great campaign against the Khitan was about to be launched, so this edict of instruction was issued.
translations.idiomatic: A major Khitan campaign was then in preparation, and this edict was sent to rally Bohai support.

sentences.zh: 九年春，宴大明殿，因召大鸞河慰撫久之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year, a banquet was held in the Hall of Great Brightness, and Daluanhe was summoned and comforted for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year nine the emperor feasted in the Hall of Great Brightness and summoned Daluanhe for a long, cordial audience.

sentences.zh: 上謂殿前都校劉延翰曰：「鸞河，渤海豪帥，束身歸我，嘉其忠順。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the Metropolitan Commander of the Hall Liu Yanhan: 'Luanhe is a heroic leader of Bohai who bound himself and came to us—I commend his loyalty and obedience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Metropolitan Commander Liu Yanhan: 'Luanhe is a Bohai chieftain who came to us of his own accord; I commend his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 夫夷落之俗，以馳騁爲樂，候高秋戒候，當與駿馬數十匹，令出郊遊獵，以遂其性。」

translations.literal: The custom of Yi settlements takes galloping as pleasure; when high autumn's season of caution arrives, he should be given several tens of fine horses and ordered to go out to the suburbs to hunt and roam, to satisfy his nature.'
translations.idiomatic: Border peoples love the chase; when autumn comes, give him several dozen fine horses and let him hunt in the countryside to his heart's content.'

sentences.zh: 因以緡錢十萬並酒賜之。

translations.literal: Thereupon one hundred thousand strings of cash and wine were bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted one hundred thousand strings of cash and wine.

sentences.zh: 日本國

translations.literal: The State of Japan.
translations.idiomatic: Japan

sentences.zh: 日本國者，本倭奴國也。

translations.literal: The State of Japan was originally the state of Woren.
translations.idiomatic: Japan was formerly known as the land of Wa.

sentences.zh: 自以其國近日所出，故以日本爲名；

translations.literal: Because their state lies where the sun emerges, they therefore take Japan as the name;
translations.idiomatic: Because their country lies where the sun rises, they took the name Japan;

sentences.zh: 或云惡其舊名改之也。

translations.literal: or it is said they disliked the old name and changed it.
translations.idiomatic: or some say they changed it because they disliked the old name.

sentences.zh: 其地東西南北各數千里，西南至海，東北隅隔以大山，山外即毛人國。

translations.literal: Its territory extends several thousand li in each direction east, west, south, and north; southwest it reaches the sea; the northeastern corner is divided by great mountains, and beyond the mountains is the state of the Hairy People.
translations.idiomatic: Its domain stretches several thousand li in every direction; to the southwest lies the sea, and in the northeast great mountains separate it from the land of the Hairy People beyond.

sentences.zh: 自後漢始朝貢，歷魏、晉、宋、隋皆來貢，唐永徽、顯慶、長安、開元、天寶、上元、貞元、元和、開成中，並遣使入朝。

translations.literal: From Later Han they first offered court tribute; through Wei, Jin, Song, and Sui they all came with tribute; in Tang during Yonghui, Xianqing, Chang'an, Kaiyuan, Tianbao, Shangyuan, Zhenyuan, Yuanhe, and Kaicheng, they all sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute began in Later Han and continued through Wei, Jin, Liu Song, and Sui; under Tang they sent embassies in the Yonghui, Xianqing, Chang'an, Kaiyuan, Tianbao, Shangyuan, Zhenyuan, Yuanhe, and Kaicheng reigns.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，日本國僧奝然與其徒五六人浮海而至，獻銅器十餘事，並本國《職員今》、《王年代紀》各一卷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi, the Japanese monk Chiran and five or six of his disciples came floating across the sea, presenting more than ten bronze objects and one roll each of their state's Offices Statute and Chronology of Kings.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 1 (984), the Japanese monk Chiran arrived by sea with five or six disciples, bearing more than ten bronze vessels and one copy each of his country's Offices Statute and Chronology of Kings.

sentences.zh: 奝然衣綠，自云姓藤原氏，父爲真連；

translations.literal: Chiran wore green robes and said his surname was Fujiwara; his father was Zhenlian;
translations.idiomatic: Chiran wore green robes and said he was of the Fujiwara clan; his father had held the rank of Zhenlian;

sentences.zh: 真連，其國五品品官也。

translations.literal: Zhenlian was a fifth-rank official of their state.
translations.idiomatic: a fifth-grade office in the Japanese court hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 奝然善隸書，而不通華言，問其風土，但書以對云：「國中有《五經》書及佛經、《白居易集》七十卷，並得自中國。

translations.literal: Chiran was skilled at clerical script but did not understand Chinese speech; when asked about their customs and land, he only wrote in reply, saying: 'In the state there are the Five Classics and Buddhist sutras and seventy rolls of the Collected Works of Bai Juyi, all obtained from China.
translations.idiomatic: Chiran wrote clerical script well but spoke no Chinese; asked about his homeland, he wrote: 'Our country has the Five Classics, Buddhist scriptures, and seventy juan of Bai Juyi's collected works, all obtained from China.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀而少麥。

translations.literal: The soil suits the five grains but has little wheat.
translations.idiomatic: The land grows the five grains well but little wheat.

sentences.zh: 交易用銅錢，文曰『乾文大寶』。

translations.literal: Trade used copper coins inscribed 'Qianwen Dabao.'
translations.idiomatic: Commerce used copper coins inscribed 'Qianwen Dabao.'

sentences.zh: 畜有水牛、驢、羊，多犀、象。

translations.literal: They kept water buffalo, donkeys, and sheep; rhinoceroses and elephants were many.
translations.idiomatic: They raised water buffalo, donkeys, and sheep, and had many rhinoceroses and elephants.

sentences.zh: 產絲蠶，多織絹，薄致可愛。

translations.literal: They produced silk and silkworms, wove much silk gauze, thin and delicate and lovely.
translations.idiomatic: Silk and silkworms were produced there, and they wove much fine, delicate gauze.

sentences.zh: 樂有中國、高麗二部。

translations.literal: In music there were Chinese and Goryeo sections.
translations.idiomatic: Their music included Chinese and Goryeo repertoires.

sentences.zh: 四時寒暑，大類中國。

translations.literal: The four seasons' cold and heat were largely like China's.
translations.idiomatic: The seasons and climate were much like China's.

sentences.zh: 國之東境接海島，夷人所居，身面皆有毛。

translations.literal: The state's eastern border adjoins sea islands where Yi people dwell, their bodies and faces all having hair.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern frontier borders islands where barbarian peoples live, hairy over face and body.

sentences.zh: 東奧州產黃金，西別島出白銀，以爲貢賦。

translations.literal: Eastern O Province produced gold; the western separate island yielded silver, used as tribute and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern O province produced gold and a western island silver, which served as tribute.

sentences.zh: 國王以王爲姓，傳襲至今王六十四世，文武僚吏皆世官。」

translations.literal: The king takes Wang as surname; succession has continued to the present king, the sixty-fourth generation; civil and military officials are all hereditary offices.'
translations.idiomatic: The royal house bears the surname Wang and has ruled through sixty-four generations to the present king; all civil and military posts are hereditary.'

sentences.zh: 其《年代紀》所記云：「初主號天御中主。

translations.literal: Its Chronology records, saying: 'The first ruler was styled Heavenly Sovereign in the Midst.
translations.idiomatic: The Chronology records: 'The first ruler was called Heavenly Sovereign in the Midst.

sentences.zh: 次曰天村雲尊，其後皆以『尊』爲號。

translations.literal: Next was Heavenly Village Cloud Lord; afterward all used 'Lord' as title.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Heavenly Village Cloud Lord; thereafter all used the title 'Lord.'

sentences.zh: 次天八重雲尊，次天彌聞尊，次天忍勝尊，次瞻波尊，次萬魂尊，次利利魂尊，次國狹槌尊，次角龔魂尊，次汲津丹尊，次面垂見尊，次國常立尊，次天鑒尊，次天萬尊，次沫名杵尊，次伊奘諾尊，次素戔烏尊，次天照大神尊，次正哉吾勝速日天押穗耳尊，次天彥尊，次炎尊，次彥瀲尊，凡二十三世，並都於築紫日向宮。

translations.literal: Next Heavenly Eightfold Cloud Lord, next Heavenly Full Hearing Lord, next Heavenly Enduring Victory Lord, next Zhanbo Lord, next Myriad Souls Lord, next Sharp Souls Lord, next Narrow Mallet of the State Lord, next Horn Gong Soul Lord, next Drawing Ford Cinnabar Lord, next Face Hanging Seen Lord, next Ever-Standing State Lord, next Heavenly Mirror Lord, next Heavenly Myriad Lord, next Foam Name Pestle Lord, next Izanagi Lord, next Susa-no-O Lord, next Great Sun Goddess Lord, next Righteous Victor Swift Sun Heavenly Rice-Ear Lord, next Heavenly Prince Lord, next Flame Lord, next Prince Lian Lord—in all twenty-three generations, all with their capital at the Hyuga Palace of Tsukushi.
translations.idiomatic: Then followed, in order, Heavenly Eightfold Cloud Lord, Heavenly Full Hearing Lord, Heavenly Enduring Victory Lord, Zhanbo Lord, Myriad Souls Lord, Sharp Souls Lord, Narrow Mallet of the State Lord, Horn Gong Soul Lord, Drawing Ford Cinnabar Lord, Face Hanging Seen Lord, Ever-Standing State Lord, Heavenly Mirror Lord, Heavenly Myriad Lord, Foam Name Pestle Lord, Izanagi, Susa-no-O, the Great Sun Goddess, Righteous Victor Swift Sun Heavenly Rice-Ear, Heavenly Prince, Flame, and Prince Lian—twenty-three reigns in all, with their capital at the Hyuga palace in Tsukushi.

sentences.zh: 彥瀲第四子號神武天皇，自築紫宮入居大和州橿原宮，即位元年甲寅，當周僖王時也。

translations.literal: The fourth son of Prince Lian was styled Emperor Jimmu; from the Tsukushi palace he entered and dwelt in the Kashihara Palace of Yamato Province; the first year of his accession was jiayin, corresponding to the time of King Xi of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lian's fourth son took the title Emperor Jimmu, moved from the Tsukushi palace to the Kashihara palace in Yamato, and acceded in the jiayin year, in the reign of King Xi of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 次綏靖天皇，次安寧天皇，次懿德天皇，次孝昭天皇，次孝天皇，次孝靈天皇，次孝元天皇，次開化天皇，次崇神天篁，次垂仁天皇，次景行天皇，次成務天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Suizei, next Emperor Annei, next Emperor Itoku, next Emperor Kosho, next Emperor Ko, next Emperor Korei, next Emperor Kogen, next Emperor Kaika, next Divine Emperor Sujin, next Emperor Suinin, next Emperor Keiko, next Emperor Seimu.
translations.idiomatic: He was followed by Emperors Suizei, Annei, Itoku, Kosho, Ko, Korei, Kogen, Kaika, Sujin, Suinin, Keiko, and Seimu.

sentences.zh: 次仲哀天皇，國人言今爲鎮國香椎大神。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Chuai; the people of the state say he is now the Great God of Kashii Who Pacifies the State.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Chuai, whom the Japanese say is now worshipped as the Great God of Kashii Who Pacifies the Realm.

sentences.zh: 次神功天皇，開化天皇之曾孫女，又謂之息長足姬天皇，國人言今爲太奈良姬大神。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Jingu, great-great-granddaughter of Emperor Kaika, also called Empress Okinaga Tarashi; the people say she is now the Great Goddess of Nara.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Empress Jingu, a great-great-granddaughter of Kaika, also called Okinaga Tarashi; the Japanese revere her today as the Great Goddess of Nara.

sentences.zh: 次應神天皇，甲辰歲，始於百濟得中國文字，今號八蕃菩薩，有大臣號紀武內，年三百七歲。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Ojin; in the jiachen year they first obtained Chinese writing from Baekje; he is now styled the Bodhisattva of the Eight Barbarians; there was a minister styled Ki no Takeuchi, age three hundred seven.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Ojin; in a jiachen year Japan first received Chinese writing from Baekje. He is now venerated as the Bodhisattva of the Eight Barbarians, and a minister named Ki no Takeuchi is said to have lived three hundred and seven years.

sentences.zh: 次仁德天皇，次履中天皇，次反正天皇，次允恭天皇，次安康天皇，次雄略天皇，次清甯天皇，次顯宗天皇，次仁賢天皇，次武烈天皇，次繼體天皇，次安開天皇，次宣化天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Nintoku, next Emperor Richu, next Emperor Hanzei, next Emperor Ingyo, next Emperor Anko, next Emperor Yuryaku, next Emperor Seinei, next Emperor Kenzo, next Emperor Ninken, next Emperor Buretsu, next Emperor Keitai, next Emperor Ankan, next Emperor Senka.
translations.idiomatic: They were followed by Emperors Nintoku, Richu, Hanzei, Ingyo, Anko, Yuryaku, Seinei, Kenzo, Ninken, Buretsu, Keitai, Ankan, and Senka.

sentences.zh: 次天國排開廣庭天皇，亦名欽明天皇，即位十三年，壬申歲始傳佛法于百濟國，當此土梁承聖元年。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Kinmei, also called Emperor Kinmei; in the thirteenth year of his reign, in the renshen year, Buddhist law was first transmitted to Baekje, corresponding to the first year of Chengsheng of Liang in this land.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Kinmei; in the thirteenth year of his reign, a renshen year, Buddhism was first sent to Baekje—the same year as Liang Chengsheng 1 in China.

sentences.zh: 次敏達天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Bidatsu.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Bidatsu.

sentences.zh: 次用明天皇，有子曰聖德太子，年三歲，聞十人語，同時解之，七歲悟佛法於菩提寺，講《聖曼經》，天雨曼陀羅華。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Yomei; he had a son called Prince Shotoku; at age three, hearing ten people speak, he understood all at once; at seven he awakened to Buddhist law at Bodhi Temple, lectured on the Shengman Sutra, and mandarava flowers rained from heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Yomei, whose son Prince Shotoku at age three could hear ten people speaking and understand them all at once; at seven he grasped the Dharma at Bodhi Temple, expounded the Shengman Sutra, and mandarava flowers fell from the sky.

sentences.zh: 當此土隋開皇中，遣使泛海至中國，求《法華經》。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui in this land, he sent envoys across the sea to China to seek the Lotus Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: During China's Sui Kaihuang era he sent envoys across the sea to obtain the Lotus Sutra.

sentences.zh: 次崇峻天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Sushun.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Sushun.

sentences.zh: 次推古天皇，欽明天皇之女也。

translations.literal: Next Empress Suiko, daughter of Emperor Kinmei.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Empress Suiko, a daughter of Kinmei.

sentences.zh: 次舒明天皇，次皇極天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Jomei, next Empress Kogyoku.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperors Jomei and Empress Kogyoku.

sentences.zh: 次孝德天皇，白雉四年，律師道照求法至中國，從三藏僧玄奘受經、律、論，當此土唐永徽四年也。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Kotoku; in the fourth year of Hakuchi the Vinaya master Dojo went to China to seek the law and received sutras, vinaya, and treatises from the Tripitaka master Xuanzang, corresponding to the fourth year of Yonghui of Tang in this land.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Kotoku; in Hakuchi 4 the vinaya master Dojo traveled to China and received sutras, vinaya, and treatises from Xuanzang—Tang Yonghui 4.

sentences.zh: 次天豐財重日足姬天皇，令僧智通等入唐求大乘法相教，當顯慶三年。

translations.literal: Next Empress Saimei ordered the monks Chitsu and others to enter Tang to seek the Mahayana Dharma-character teaching, corresponding to the third year of Xianqing.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Saimei then sent monks including Chitsu to Tang for the Mahayana Faxiang teaching—in Xianqing 3.

sentences.zh: 次天智天皇，次天武天皇，次持總天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Tenji, next Emperor Tenmu, next Empress Jito.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Emperors Tenji and Tenmu and Empress Jito.

sentences.zh: 次文武天皇，大寶三年，當長安元年，遣粟田真人入唐求書籍，律師道慈求經。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Monmu; in the third year of Taiho, corresponding to the first year of Chang'an, he sent Awata no Mahito to Tang to seek books, and the Vinaya master Doji to seek sutras.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Monmu; in Taiho 3 (Chang'an 1) he sent Awata no Mahito to Tang for books and the vinaya master Doji for scriptures.

sentences.zh: 次阿閉天皇，次皈依天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Shomu, next Emperor Konin.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperors Shomu and Konin.

sentences.zh: 次聖武天皇，寶龜二年，遣僧正玄昉入朝，當開元四年。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Shomu; in the second year of Hoki he sent the Sangha Lord Genbo to court, corresponding to the fourth year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Shomu; in Hoki 2 he sent the sangha lord Genbo to the Tang court—Kaiyuan 4.

sentences.zh: 次孝明天皇，聖武天皇之女也，天平勝寶四年，當天寶中，遣使及僧入唐求內外經教及傳戒。

translations.literal: Next Empress Kōken, daughter of Emperor Shōmu; in the fourth year of Tenpyō Shōhō, corresponding to the Tianbao era, she sent envoys and monks to Tang to seek inner and outer scriptures and the transmission of precepts.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Empress Kōken, a daughter of Emperor Shōmu; in Tenpyō Shōhō 4, during the Tang Tianbao era, she sent envoys and monks to Tang for Buddhist scriptures and ordination.

sentences.zh: 次天炊天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Tenkasui.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Tenkasui.

sentences.zh: 次高野姬天皇，聖武天皇之女也。

translations.literal: Next Empress Genshō, daughter of Emperor Shōmu.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Empress Genshō, another daughter of Emperor Shōmu.

sentences.zh: 次白璧天皇，二十四年，遣二僧靈仙、行賀入唐，禮五臺山學佛法。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Heizei; in his twenty-fourth year he sent two monks, Ryōsen and Gyōga, to Tang to worship Mount Wutai and study Buddhist law.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Heizei; in his twenty-fourth year he sent the monks Ryōsen and Gyōga to Tang to pay reverence at Mount Wutai and study the Dharma.

sentences.zh: 次桓武天皇，遣騰元葛野與空海大師及延曆寺僧澄入唐，詣天臺山傳智者止觀義，當元和元年也。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Kammu; he sent Tōgen Kadono together with the Great Master Kūkai and the monk Chō of Enryaku-ji to Tang, proceeding to Mount Tiantai to transmit the stop-and-contemplation doctrine of Zhiyi, corresponding to the first year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Kammu, who sent Tōgen Kadono with the Great Master Kūkai and the Enryaku-ji monk Chō to Tang and on to Mount Tiantai to bring back Zhiyi's doctrine of śamatha-vipaśyanā—in Yuanhe 1.

sentences.zh: 次諾樂天皇，次嵯峨天皇，次淳和天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Noraku, next Emperor Saga, next Emperor Junna.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Emperors Noraku, Saga, and Junna.

sentences.zh: 次仁明天皇，當開成、會昌中，遣僧入唐，禮五台。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Ninmyō; during the Kaicheng and Huichang eras he sent monks to Tang to worship Mount Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Ninmyō; in the Kaicheng and Huichang eras he sent monks to Tang to worship Mount Wutai.

sentences.zh: 次文德天皇，當大中年間。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Montoku; during the Dazhong period.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Montoku, in the Dazhong era.

sentences.zh: 次清和天皇，次陽成天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Seiwa, next Emperor Yōzei.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Emperors Seiwa and Yōzei.

sentences.zh: 次光孝天皇，遣僧宗睿入唐傳教，當光啟元年也。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Kōkō; he sent the monk Shūei to Tang to transmit the teaching, corresponding to the first year of Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Kōkō, who sent the monk Shūei to Tang to spread the teaching—in Guangqi 1.

sentences.zh: 次仁和天皇，當此土梁龍德中，遣僧寬建等入朝。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Ninna; during Longde of Liang in this land he sent the monk Kanken and others to court.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Ninna; during Liang Longde he sent the monk Kanken and others to the Chinese court.

sentences.zh: 次醍醐天皇，次天慶天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Daigo, next Emperor Tenkei.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Emperors Daigo and Tenkei.

sentences.zh: 次封上天皇，當此土周廣順年也。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Fuzhang; corresponding to the Guangshun years of Zhou in this land.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Fuzhang, in the Zhou Guangshun era.

sentences.zh: 次冷泉天皇，今爲太上天皇。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Reizei; he is now retired emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Reizei, who now reigns as retired emperor.

sentences.zh: 次守平天皇，即今王也。

translations.literal: Next Emperor Heizei; he is the present king.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Emperor Heizei, the reigning sovereign.

sentences.zh: 凡六十四世。

translations.literal: In all, sixty-four generations.
translations.idiomatic: In all there had been sixty-four sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 畿內有山城、大和、河內、和泉、攝津凡五州，共統五十三郡。

translations.literal: Within the capital region were Yamashiro, Yamato, Kawachi, Izumi, and Settsu—five provinces in all, together governing fifty-three districts.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region comprised five provinces—Yamashiro, Yamato, Kawachi, Izumi, and Settsu—administering fifty-three districts in all.

sentences.zh: 東海道有伊賀、伊勢、志摩、尾張、三河、遠江、駿河、伊豆、甲斐、相模、武藏、安房、上總、常陸凡十四州，共統一百一十六郡。

translations.literal: The Tōkaidō had Iga, Ise, Shima, Owari, Mikawa, Tōtōmi, Suruga, Izu, Kai, Sagami, Musashi, Awa, Kazusa, and Hitachi—fourteen provinces in all, together governing one hundred sixteen districts.
translations.idiomatic: The Tōkaidō comprised fourteen provinces—Iga, Ise, Shima, Owari, Mikawa, Tōtōmi, Suruga, Izu, Kai, Sagami, Musashi, Awa, Kazusa, and Hitachi—administering one hundred sixteen districts.

sentences.zh: 東山道有通江、美濃、飛驒、信濃、上野、下野、陸奧、出羽凡八州，共統一百二十二郡。

translations.literal: The Tōsandō had Tongjiang, Mino, Hida, Shinano, Kōzuke, Shimotsuke, Mutsu, and Dewa—eight provinces in all, together governing one hundred twenty-two districts.
translations.idiomatic: The Tōsandō comprised eight provinces—Omi, Mino, Hida, Shinano, Kōzuke, Shimotsuke, Mutsu, and Dewa—administering one hundred twenty-two districts.

sentences.zh: 北陸道有若狹、越前、加賀、能登、越中、越後、佐渡凡七州，共統三十郡。

translations.literal: The Hokurikudō had Wakasa, Echizen, Kaga, Noto, Etchū, Echigo, and Sado—seven provinces in all, together governing thirty districts.
translations.idiomatic: The Hokurikudō comprised seven provinces—Wakasa, Echizen, Kaga, Noto, Etchū, Echigo, and Sado—administering thirty districts.

sentences.zh: 山陰道有丹波、丹彼、徂馬、因幡、伯耆、出雲、石見、隱伎凡八州，共統五十二郡。

translations.literal: The San'indō had Tanba, Tanhi, Zuma, Inaba, Hōki, Izumo, Iwami, and Ingi—eight provinces in all, together governing fifty-two districts.
translations.idiomatic: The San'indō comprised eight provinces—Tanba, Tajima, Inaba, Hōki, Izumo, Iwami, and Oki, with one province name corrupted in the source—administering fifty-two districts.

sentences.zh: 小陽道有播麼、美作、備前、備中、備後、安藝、周防、長門凡八州，共統六十九郡。

translations.literal: The Xiaoyangdō had Harima, Mimasaka, Bizen, Bitchū, Bingo, Aki, Suō, and Nagato—eight provinces in all, together governing sixty-nine districts.
translations.idiomatic: The Sanyōdō comprised eight provinces—Harima, Mimasaka, Bizen, Bitchū, Bingo, Aki, Suō, and Nagato—administering sixty-nine districts.

sentences.zh: 南海道有伊紀、淡路、河波、贊耆、伊豫、土佐凡六州，共統四十八郡。

translations.literal: The Nankaidō had Iki, Awaji, Hebo, Sanqi, Iyo, and Tosa—six provinces in all, together governing forty-eight districts.
translations.idiomatic: The Nankaidō comprised six provinces—Kii, Awaji, Awa, Sanuki, Iyo, and Tosa—administering forty-eight districts.

sentences.zh: 西海道有築前、築後、豐前、豐後、肥前、肥後、日向、大隅、薩摩凡九州，共統九十三郡。

translations.literal: The Saikaidō had Chikuzen, Chikugo, Buzen, Bungo, Hizen, Higo, Hyūga, Ōsumi, and Satsuma—nine provinces in all, together governing ninety-three districts.
translations.idiomatic: The Saikaidō comprised nine provinces—Chikuzen, Chikugo, Buzen, Bungo, Hizen, Higo, Hyūga, Ōsumi, and Satsuma—administering ninety-three districts.

sentences.zh: 又有壹伎、對馬、多礻執凡三島，各統二郡。

translations.literal: There were also Iki, Tsushima, and Duozhi - three islands in all, each governing two districts.
translations.idiomatic: There were also three outlying islands - Iki, Tsushima, and a third island whose name is corrupt in the manuscript - each administering two districts.

sentences.zh: 是謂五畿、七道、三島，凡三千七百七十二都，四百一十四驛，八十八萬三千三百二十九課丁。

translations.literal: These are called the Five Capital Provinces, Seven Circuits, and Three Islands—in all 3,772 districts, 414 post stations, and 883,329 taxable males.
translations.idiomatic: This was the realm of the Five Capital Provinces, Seven Circuits, and Three Islands: 3,772 districts, 414 relay stations, and 883,329 registered tax-paying males.

sentences.zh: 課丁之外，不可詳見。

translations.literal: Beyond the taxable males, details cannot be fully seen.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the registered tax males, the rest of the population could not be ascertained in detail.

sentences.zh: 皆奝然所記雲。

translations.literal: All were recorded by Chiran, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: All of this, it is said, was recorded by Chiran.

sentences.zh: 按隋開皇二十年，倭王姓阿每，名自多利思比孤，遣使致書。

translations.literal: According to the records, in the twentieth year of Kaihuang of Sui, the Wa king surnamed Ame, named Ametarishiko, sent envoys with a letter.
translations.idiomatic: Records show that in Sui Kaihuang 20 the Wa king Ametarishiko, of the Ame clan, sent envoys bearing a letter.

sentences.zh: 唐永徽五年，遣使獻琥珀、馬腦。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui of Tang, envoys were sent presenting amber and agate.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Yonghui 5 they sent envoys bearing tribute of amber and agate.

sentences.zh: 長安二年，遣其朝臣真人貢方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an, they sent their courtier Mahito to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an 2 they sent the courtier Mahito with regional tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遣使來朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, envoys were sent to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Kaiyuan era they sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 天寶十二年，又遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianbao, envoys were again sent to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 12 they again sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，遣高階真人來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe, Takashina no Mahito was sent to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 1 they sent Takashina no Mahito with tribute.

sentences.zh: 開成四年，又遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaicheng, envoys were again sent to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 4 they again sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 此與其所記皆同。

translations.literal: This and what he recorded are all the same.
translations.idiomatic: These entries accord with what Chiran recorded.

sentences.zh: 大中、光啟、龍德及周廣順中，皆嘗遣僧至中國，《唐書》中、《五代史》失其傳。

translations.literal: During Dazhong, Guangqi, Longde, and the Guangshun years of Zhou, monks were all once sent to China; the Tang History has them, the Five Dynasties History lacks their transmission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong, Guangqi, and Longde eras and the Zhou Guangshun reign, monks had also been sent to China—the Tang History mentions them, but the Five Dynasties History omits the record.

sentences.zh: 唐咸亨中及開元二十三年、大曆十二年、建中元年，皆來朝貢，其記不載。

translations.literal: During Xianheng of Tang, and in the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, the twelfth year of Dali, and the first year of Jianzhong, all came to court with tribute; his record does not include them.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute missions also came in Tang Xianheng, Kaiyuan 23, Dali 12, and Jianzhong 1—none of which appear in Chiran's account.

sentences.zh: 太宗召見奝然，存撫之甚厚，賜紫衣，館于太平興國寺。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong summoned and received Chiran, treated him with great kindness and consolation, bestowed purple robes, and lodged him at Taiping Xingguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong received Chiran in audience, treated him with exceptional kindness, granted him purple robes, and housed him at Taiping Xingguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 上聞其國王一姓傳繼，臣下皆世官，因歎息謂宰相曰：「此島夷耳，乃世祚遐久，其臣亦繼襲不絕，此蓋古之道也。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that in their state the kings were transmitted within one surname and the ministers all held hereditary offices; he therefore sighed and said to the chief ministers: 'These are only island barbarians, yet their royal line endures through distant ages and their ministers too succeed without break—this must be the way of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Japan's throne passed within a single clan and its ministers held hereditary office, the emperor sighed and told his chief ministers, 'They are only islanders, yet their dynasty has endured for ages and ministerial lines continue unbroken—surely this is the way of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 中國自唐季之亂，宇縣分裂，梁、周五代享曆尤促，大臣世胄，鮮能嗣續。

translations.literal: Since the disorders at the end of Tang in China, the realm has been divided; Liang and Zhou, the Five Dynasties, enjoyed reigns especially brief, and great ministers of hereditary houses have rarely been able to continue their lines.
translations.idiomatic: Since the chaos at the end of Tang, China itself has been torn apart; under Liang and Zhou the Five Dynasties ruled only briefly, and great ministerial houses have seldom kept their lines intact.

sentences.zh: 朕雖德慚往聖，常夙夜寅畏，講求治本，不敢暇逸。

translations.literal: Although We are shamed in virtue before the sages of old, We constantly from early morning to late night hold reverent fear, seek the root of governance, and dare not be idle.
translations.idiomatic: Though I fall short of the sages of old, I rise early and retire late in reverent diligence, striving for sound governance and daring not to slacken.

sentences.zh: 建無窮之業，垂可久之範，亦以爲子孫之計，使大臣之後世襲祿位，此朕之心焉。」

translations.literal: To establish an enterprise without end and leave a lasting model is also to plan for Our descendants, so that the descendants of great ministers may hereditarily inherit rank and stipend—this is Our intent.'
translations.idiomatic: I mean to build an enduring foundation and leave a lasting example—not least for my heirs—so that ministers' sons may inherit office and emolument in turn. That is my aim.'

sentences.zh: 其國多有中國典籍，奝然之來，復得《孝經》一卷、越王《孝經新義》第十五一卷，皆金縷紅羅標，水晶爲軸。

translations.literal: Their state has many Chinese classics; with Chiran's coming they again obtained one roll of the Classic of Filial Piety and one roll, the fifteenth, of the Prince of Yue's New Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety—all with gold-threaded red silk labels and crystal rollers.
translations.idiomatic: Japan already held many Chinese classics; with Chiran's visit the court also received a copy of the Classic of Filial Piety and juan 15 of the Prince of Yue's New Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety, each bound with gold-threaded red silk labels and crystal rollers.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》即鄭氏注者。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety was the one with Zheng's commentary.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety was the edition with Zheng's commentary.

sentences.zh: 越王者，乃唐太宗子越王貞；

translations.literal: The Prince of Yue was the son of Emperor Taizong of Tang, Prince Zhen of Yue;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yue was Prince Zhen, a son of Emperor Taizong of Tang;

sentences.zh: 《新義》者，記室參軍任希古等撰也。

translations.literal: the New Meaning was compiled by the secretariat officer Ren Xigu and others.
translations.idiomatic: and the New Meaning had been compiled by the secretariat officer Ren Xigu and others.

sentences.zh: 奝然復求詣五台，許之，令所過續食；

translations.literal: Chiran again requested to proceed to Mount Wutai; permission was granted, and he was ordered to be supplied with continued provisions along the route;
translations.idiomatic: Chiran asked to visit Mount Wutai as well; the emperor consented and ordered provisions supplied at every stage of the journey;

sentences.zh: 又求印本《大藏經》，詔亦給之。

translations.literal: he also requested a printed edition of the Great Canon, and an edict likewise granted it.
translations.idiomatic: he also requested a printed edition of the Buddhist canon, and an edict granted that too.

sentences.zh: 二年，隨台州甯海縣商人鄭仁德船歸其國。

translations.literal: In the second year, he returned to his state aboard the ship of the merchant Zheng Rende of Ninghai County in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he sailed home on the ship of Zheng Rende, a merchant of Ninghai County in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 後數年，仁德還。

translations.literal: Several years later, Rende returned.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Rende returned.

sentences.zh: 奝然遣其弟子喜因奉表來謝曰：「日本國東大寺大朝法濟大師、賜紫、沙門奝然啟：傷鱗入夢，不忘漢主之恩；

translations.literal: Chiran sent his disciple Ki'in to present a memorial in thanks, saying: 'The Great Master of the Dharma and Salvation of the Great Court of Japan's Eastern Great Temple, purple robe bestowed, śrāmaṇa Chiran submits: A wounded fish entering a dream does not forget the Han emperor's grace;
translations.idiomatic: Chiran sent his disciple Ki'in with a memorial of thanks that read: 'The Great Master of the Dharma and Salvation of the Great Court of Japan's Eastern Great Temple, purple-robed śrāmaṇa Chiran respectfully submits: Like a wounded fish appearing in a dream, I cannot forget the grace of the Han emperor;

sentences.zh: 枯骨合歡，猶亢魏氏之敵。

translations.literal: dry bones joined in joy still resist the enemy of the house of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: like dry bones reunited in joy, I still hold firm against the foe of Wei;

sentences.zh: 雖雲羊僧之拙，誰忍鴻霈之誠。

translations.literal: Although one may say this sheepish monk is clumsy, who could bear to reject the sincerity of vast imperial favor?
translations.idiomatic: Humble though this rustic monk may be, who could refuse the sincerity of so vast an imperial favor?

sentences.zh: 奝然誠惶誠恐，頓首頓首，死罪。

translations.literal: Chiran is truly fearful and truly trembling, kowtowing, kowtowing—worthy of death.
translations.idiomatic: Chiran prostrates himself in deepest awe and fear—worthy of death.

sentences.zh: 奝然附商船之離岸，期魏闕於生涯，望落日而西行，十萬里之波濤難盡；

translations.literal: Chiran, attaching himself to a merchant ship leaving shore, set his life's hope on the Wei court; gazing at the setting sun he traveled westward, and a hundred thousand li of waves were hard to exhaust;
translations.idiomatic: Chiran boarded a merchant ship bound westward, setting his life's hope on the imperial court; with the setting sun at his back he crossed seas whose hundred-thousand-li waves seemed endless;

sentences.zh: 顧信風而東別，數千里之山嶽易過。

translations.literal: then, trusting the fair wind, he parted eastward, and several thousand li of mountains and peaks were easily passed.
translations.idiomatic: yet on the homeward breeze the thousands of li of mountains were swiftly left behind.

sentences.zh: 妄以下根之卑，適詣中華之盛。

translations.literal: Presumptuously, with my lowly root-nature, I happened to arrive at the splendor of central Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Presumptuously, with my humble capacity, I came into the splendor of China.

sentences.zh: 於是宣旨頻降，恣許荒外之跋涉；

translations.literal: Thereupon imperial pronouncements descended again and again, freely permitting this journey beyond the wild frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Again and again imperial edicts descended, freely permitting this journey from beyond the seas;

sentences.zh: 宿心克協，粗觀宇內之瑰奇。

translations.literal: my long-cherished wish was fulfilled, and I roughly beheld the marvels within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: my long-cherished wish was fulfilled, and I beheld something of the wonders of the realm.

sentences.zh: 況乎金闕曉後，望堯雲於九禁之中；

translations.literal: How much more, after dawn at the golden gate-tower, to gaze upon Yao's clouds within the nine forbidden precincts;
translations.idiomatic: Above all, after dawn at the golden palace gates I beheld Yao's clouds within the innermost precincts;

sentences.zh: 岩扃晴前，拜聖燈於五台之上。

translations.literal: before the rocky gate in clear weather, to bow before the holy lamps atop Mount Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: and in clear weather before the rocky gates I bowed before the holy lamps atop Mount Wutai.

sentences.zh: 就三藏而稟學，巡數寺而優遊。

translations.literal: I drew near the Tripitaka masters to receive instruction and wandered at leisure through several monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: I studied under masters of the Tripitaka and wandered freely among many temples.

sentences.zh: 遂使蓮華回文，神筆出於北闕之北；

translations.literal: Thus the lotus sutra in reverse script and the divine brush issued from north of the northern gate;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Lotus Sutra in palindrome script and the divine brush came forth from north of the northern gate;

sentences.zh: 貝葉印字，佛詔傳於東海之東。

translations.literal: palm-leaf pages with printed characters—the Buddha's edicts were transmitted to the east of the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: and printed palm-leaf pages—the Buddha's edicts—were carried to the lands east of the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 重蒙宣恩，忽趁來跡。

translations.literal: Again receiving proclaimed grace, I suddenly hastened back along the path I had come.
translations.idiomatic: Granted imperial favor once more, I hastened home by the route I had come.

sentences.zh: 季夏解台州之纜，孟秋達本國之郊。

translations.literal: In the last month of summer I cast off the mooring lines at Taizhou; in the first month of autumn I reached the outskirts of my native state.
translations.idiomatic: In late summer I cast off from Taizhou; by early autumn I reached my homeland's shores.

sentences.zh: 爰逮明春，初到舊邑，緇素欣待，侯伯慕迎。

translations.literal: Then, reaching bright spring, I first arrived at my old district; black-robed and white-robed alike waited in joy, and marquis and earl eagerly came to welcome.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, when I first returned to my old home, monks and laypeople alike rejoiced in anticipation, and lords came eagerly to welcome me.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下惠溢四溟，恩高五嶽，世超黃、軒之古，人直金輪之新。

translations.literal: Bowingly considering that Your Majesty's kindness overflows the four seas and grace rises higher than the Five Peaks, surpassing the antiquity of the Yellow Emperor and Xuanyuan, and aligning with the new age of the golden wheel-turning king.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's kindness overflows the four seas and your grace towers above the Five Peaks; your reign surpasses the age of the Yellow Emperor and accords with the new era of the wheel-turning king.

sentences.zh: 奝然空辭鳳凰之窟，更還螻蟻之封。

translations.literal: Chiran has vainly left the phoenix's cavern and returned again to the domain of ants.
translations.idiomatic: Chiran has left the phoenix's realm and returned once more to his humble ant's domain.

sentences.zh: 在彼在斯，只仰皇德之盛；

translations.literal: Whether there or here, I can only look up to the splendor of imperial virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Whether abroad or at home, I can only look up to the splendor of your imperial virtue;

sentences.zh: 越山越海，敢忘帝念之深。

translations.literal: crossing mountains and crossing seas, how dare I forget the depth of the emperor's regard?
translations.idiomatic: across mountains and seas alike, how dare I forget the depth of your regard?

sentences.zh: 縱粉百年之身，何報一日之惠。

translations.literal: Even were I to crumble this body of a hundred years, how could I repay one day's favor?
translations.idiomatic: Even were my body to crumble over a hundred years, I could not repay a single day's grace.

sentences.zh: 染筆拭淚，伸紙搖魂，不勝慕恩之至。

translations.literal: Staining the brush and wiping tears, extending the paper and trembling the soul—I cannot bear the utmost of grateful longing for grace.
translations.idiomatic: With ink-stained brush and tears wiped away, I spread this paper with a trembling soul, overcome by gratitude.

sentences.zh: 謹差上足弟子傳燈大法師位嘉因、並大朝剃頭受戒僧祚乾等拜表以聞。」

translations.literal: Respectfully dispatching my chief disciple, the Dharma Master of the Lamp-Transmission in Great Master rank Ka'in, together with the tonsured and ordained monk Soken of the Great Court and others to bow in this memorial and report.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully I send my chief disciple, the lamp-transmission Dharma Master Ka'in, together with the tonsured and ordained monk Soken of the Great Court and others to present this memorial.'

sentences.zh: 稱其本國永延二年歲次戊子二月八日，實端拱元年也。

translations.literal: It stated that in their state, the second year of Eien, year cycle wuzi, the eighth day of the second month, was in fact the first year of Duan Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was dated the eighth day of the second month of Eien 2 (wuzi) in Japan—the same year as Duan Gong 1.

sentences.zh: 又別啟，貢佛經，納青木函；

translations.literal: There was also a separate memorial presenting Buddhist scriptures, placed in a green-wood case;
translations.idiomatic: A separate memorial accompanied the tribute: Buddhist scriptures in a green-wood case;

sentences.zh: 琥珀、青紅白水晶、紅黑木槵子念珠各一連，並納螺鈿花形平函；

translations.literal: amber, blue, red, and white crystal, and red and black wood-bead prayer rosaries, one string each, all placed in flat cases inlaid with mother-of-pearl in floral patterns;
translations.idiomatic: amber, blue, red, and white crystal, and red and black wood-bead rosaries, one string each, all in flat mother-of-pearl inlaid cases;

sentences.zh: 毛籠一，納螺杯二口；

translations.literal: one hair-woven basket, containing two conch cups;
translations.idiomatic: one wicker basket holding two conch cups;

sentences.zh: 葛籠一，納法螺二口，染皮二十枚；

translations.literal: one kudzu-woven basket, containing two dharma conch shells and twenty pieces of dyed leather;
translations.idiomatic: one kudzu basket holding two ritual conch trumpets and twenty pieces of dyed leather;

sentences.zh: 金銀蒔繪筥一合，納發鬘二頭，又一合，納參議正四位上藤佐理手書二卷、及進奉物數一卷、表狀一卷；

translations.literal: one gold-and-silver makie box, containing two sets of hair ornaments; and another box, containing two hand-written rolls by the Councilor of the Fourth Rank Upper Fujiwara no Sukemasa, together with one roll listing tribute items and one memorial;
translations.idiomatic: one gold-and-silver makie box with two sets of hair ornaments; and another box containing two autograph rolls by Councilor Fujiwara no Sukemasa, Fourth Rank Upper, plus one roll listing tribute items and one memorial;

sentences.zh: 又金銀蒔繪硯一筥一合，納金硯一、鹿毛筆、松煙墨、金銅水瓶、鐵刀；

translations.literal: also one gold-and-silver makie inkstone box, containing one gold inkstone, a deer-hair brush, pine-soot ink, a gold-copper water bottle, and an iron knife;
translations.idiomatic: also a gold-and-silver makie writing set with a gold inkstone, deer-hair brush, pine-soot ink, gilt-copper water flask, and iron knife;

sentences.zh: 又金銀蒔繪扇筥一合，納檜扇二十枚、蝙蝠扇二枚；

translations.literal: also one gold-and-silver makie fan box, containing twenty cypress fans and two bat-shaped fans;
translations.idiomatic: also a gold-and-silver makie fan case with twenty cypress fans and two bat-shaped fans;

sentences.zh: 螺鈿梳函一對，其一納赤木梳二百七十，其一納龍骨十橛；

translations.literal: one pair of mother-of-pearl inlaid comb cases, one containing two hundred seventy red-wood combs, the other containing ten pieces of dragon bone;
translations.idiomatic: a pair of mother-of-pearl comb cases—one with two hundred seventy red-wood combs, the other with ten pieces of dragon bone;

sentences.zh: 螺鈿書案一、螺鈿書幾一；

translations.literal: one mother-of-pearl inlaid writing desk and one mother-of-pearl inlaid writing table;
translations.idiomatic: one mother-of-pearl writing desk and one mother-of-pearl writing table;

sentences.zh: 金銀蒔繪平筥一合，納白細布五匹；

translations.literal: one gold-and-silver makie flat box, containing five bolts of fine white cloth;
translations.idiomatic: one gold-and-silver makie flat case with five bolts of fine white cloth;

sentences.zh: 鹿皮籠一，納䝚裘一領；

translations.literal: one deerskin basket, containing one fur robe;
translations.idiomatic: one deerskin basket holding one fur robe;

sentences.zh: 螺鈿鞍轡一副，銅鐵鐙、紅絲秋、泥障；

translations.literal: one set of mother-of-pearl inlaid saddle and bridle, with bronze-iron stirrups, red silk tassels, and mud screens;
translations.idiomatic: one mother-of-pearl saddle and bridle set with bronze-iron stirrups, red silk trappings, and mud screens;

sentences.zh: 倭畫屏風一雙；

translations.literal: one pair of Japanese-painted folding screens;
translations.idiomatic: one pair of Japanese-painted folding screens;

sentences.zh: 石流黃七百斤。

translations.literal: Seven hundred jin of sulfur.
translations.idiomatic: and seven hundred jin of sulfur.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，有僧誠尋至台州，止天臺國清寺，願留。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining, the monk Jōjin arrived at Taizhou and stayed at Tiantai Guoqing Temple, wishing to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 5 the monk Jōjin reached Taizhou and lodged at Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai, asking to remain.

sentences.zh: 州以聞，詔使赴闕。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported it, and an edict ordered him to proceed to court.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported this, and an edict summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 誠尋獻銀香爐，木槵子、白琉璃、五香、水精、紫檀、琥珀所飾念珠，及青色織物綾。

translations.literal: Jōjin presented a silver incense burner, prayer beads adorned with wood-bead, white glass, five spices, crystal, red sandalwood, and amber, and blue woven silk gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Jōjin presented a silver incense burner, prayer beads inlaid with wood-bead, white glass, five spices, crystal, red sandalwood, and amber, and bolts of blue woven silk gauze.

sentences.zh: 神宗以其遠人而有戒業，處之開寶寺，盡賜同來僧紫方袍。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong, because he was a man from afar who possessed the discipline, lodged him at Kaibao Temple and fully bestowed purple square robes on all the monks who had come with him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong, impressed that this foreigner observed the precepts, housed him at Kaibao Temple and granted purple monastic robes to all the monks who had accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 是後連貢方物，而來者皆僧也。

translations.literal: After this tribute goods were sent in succession, and those who came were all monks.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute arrived in succession, and every envoy was a monk.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，使通事僧仲回來，賜號慕化懷德大師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng, the envoy, the Interpreter Monk Chōkai, came; he was granted the title Great Master Who Cherishes Transformation and Holds Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanfeng the interpreter monk Chōkai arrived and was granted the title Great Master Who Cherishes Transformation and Holds Virtue.

sentences.zh: 明州又言得其國太宰府牒，因使人孫忠還，遣仲回等貢絁二百匹、水銀五千兩，以孫忠乃海商，而貢禮與諸國異，請自移牒報，而答其物直，付仲回東歸。

translations.literal: Mingzhou also reported obtaining a dispatch from their state's Dazaifu; because the envoy Sun Zhong was returning, Chōkai and others were sent presenting two hundred bolts of silk and five thousand liang of mercury; since Sun Zhong was a sea merchant and the tribute rites differed from other states, it was requested that a reply dispatch be sent independently, that the value of the goods be returned in payment, and that this be entrusted to Chōkai for the eastward return.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhou also reported receiving a dispatch from Japan's Dazaifu office. Because the merchant Sun Zhong was returning, Chōkai and others brought two hundred bolts of silk and five thousand liang of mercury as tribute. Since Sun Zhong was a private sea trader and Japan's tribute protocol differed from that of other states, the court requested permission to reply with its own dispatch, compensate the goods at market value, and entrust payment to Chōkai for his return eastward.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 乾道九年，始附明州綱首以方物入貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qiandao, they first attached themselves to the convoy leader of Mingzhou to enter tribute with local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 9 they first sent tribute goods by joining a Mingzhou convoy leader.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，倭船火兒滕太明毆鄭作死，詔械太明付其綱首歸，治以其國之法。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi, the Japanese sailor Teng Taiming of a ship's crew beat Zheng Zuo to death; an edict ordered Taiming shackled and handed to his convoy leader for return, to be punished according to the laws of his state.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 2 the Japanese sailor Teng Taiming of a ship's crew beat Zheng Zuo to death; an edict ordered Taiming shackled and handed to his convoy leader for repatriation, to be punished under Japanese law.

sentences.zh: 三年，風泊日本舟至明州，衆皆不得食，行乞至臨安府者復百餘人。

translations.literal: In the third year, a Japanese ship driven ashore by wind arrived at Mingzhou; all were without food, and again more than a hundred people begged their way as far as Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 3 a Japanese ship blown ashore reached Mingzhou; the crew had no food, and more than a hundred of them resorted to begging as far as Lin'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔人日給錢五十文、米二升，俟其國舟至日遣歸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that each person be given daily fifty cash and two sheng of rice, and that they be sent home when their state's ship arrived.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted each person fifty cash and two sheng of rice per day and ordered that they be repatriated when a ship from Japan arrived.

sentences.zh: 十年，日本七十三人復飄至秀州華亭縣，給常平義倉錢米以振之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, seventy-three Japanese again drifted ashore at Huating County in Xiuzhou; Changping and Ever-Normal Granary funds and grain were issued to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 10 seventy-three Japanese were again cast ashore at Huating County in Xiuzhou; relief was paid from Changping and Ever-Normal Granary stores.

sentences.zh: 紹熙四年，泰州及秀州華亭縣復有倭人爲風所泊而至者，詔勿取其貨，出常平米振給而遣之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi, again in Taizhou and Huating County in Xiuzhou there were Wa people who arrived driven ashore by wind; an edict ordered that their goods not be taken, that Ever-Normal Granary rice be issued in relief, and that they be sent away.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 4 Japanese cast ashore again at Taizhou and at Huating in Xiuzhou; an edict forbade seizing their goods, supplied relief rice from the Ever-Normal Granary, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 慶元六年至平江府，嘉泰二年至定海縣，詔並給錢米遣歸國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qingyuan they reached Pingjiang Prefecture; in the second year of Jiatai they reached Dinghai County; an edict ordered that money and grain be given to all and that they be sent back to their state.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingyuan 6 some reached Pingjiang Prefecture and in Jiatai 2 others reached Dinghai County; an edict provided money and grain and sent them all home.

sentences.zh: 党項，古析支之地，漢西羌之別種。

translations.literal: The Tangut occupied the ancient land of Qizhi; they were a separate stock of the Western Qiang of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut lived in the ancient territory of Qizhi and were a branch of the Western Qiang known since Han times.

sentences.zh: 後周世始強盛，有細風氏、費聽氏、往利氏、頗超氏、野亂氏、房當氏、來禽氏、拓拔氏最爲強族。

translations.literal: From the Later Zhou they first grew powerful; the Xifeng, Feiting, Wangli, Pochao, Yeluan, Fangdang, Laiqin, and Tuoba clans were the strongest tribes.
translations.idiomatic: They first rose to power under the Later Zhou; the Xifeng, Feiting, Wangli, Pochao, Yeluan, Fangdang, Laiqin, and Tuoba were the most powerful clans.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀至上元間內附，散居西北邊。

translations.literal: Between the Zhenguan and Shangyuan reigns of Tang they submitted and were scattered along the northwest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang Zhenguan through Shangyuan they submitted to the court and settled across the northwestern frontier.

sentences.zh: 元和以後，頗相率爲盜。

translations.literal: After Yuanhe, they frequently banded together as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuanhe era they often banded together in raids.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，武宗置三使以統之：在邠、寧、延者爲一使，在鹽、夏、長澤者爲一使，在靈武、麟、勝者爲一使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang, Wuzong established three commissioners to govern them: those in Bian, Ning, and Yan formed one commissioner, those in Yan, Xia, and Changze another, and those in Lingwu, Lin, and Sheng another.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huichang Emperor Wuzong placed them under three commissioners: one over the Bian-Ning-Yan region, one over Yan-Xia-Changze, and one over Lingwu-Lin-Sheng.

sentences.zh: 五代亦嘗入貢。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties they also at times sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Five Dynasties they sometimes sent tribute as well.

sentences.zh: 今靈、夏、綏、麟、府、環、慶、豐州，鎮戎、天德、振武軍並其族帳。

translations.literal: Today Ling, Xia, Sui, Lin, Fu, Huan, Qing, and Feng prefectures, together with Zhenrong, Tiande, and Zhenwu garrisons, all contain their tribal encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribal encampments now lay across Ling, Xia, Sui, Lin, Fu, Huan, Qing, and Feng prefectures and the garrisons of Zhenrong, Tiande, and Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆二年，代州刺史折乜埋來朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong under Taizu, Zhe Miemai, prefect of Daizhou, came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2, Daiz Prefect Zhe Miemai came to court.

sentences.zh: 乜埋，党項之大姓，世居河右，有捍邊之功，故授以方州，召令入覲而遣還。

translations.literal: Miemai was a great Tangut surname; for generations they dwelt west of the Yellow River and had merit in defending the frontier, and so he was granted a prefecture, summoned to audience, and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Miemai was a leading Tangut clan that had long held the west-of-the-River country and distinguished itself on the frontier; he was therefore given a prefecture, summoned to audience, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 開寶元年，直蕩族首領啜佶等引並人寇府州，爲王師所敗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaibao, the Zhidang chieftain Chuo Ji and others led Bing troops to raid Fuzhou and were defeated by the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 1 the Zhidang chieftain Chuo Ji and others led Bing forces in a raid on Fu Prefecture and were defeated by imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 詔內屬羌部十六府大首領屈遇與十二府首領羅崖領所部誅啜佶，啜佶懼，以其族歸順。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qu Yu, great chieftain of the sixteen prefectures of the affiliated Qiang, and Luo Ya, chieftain of twelve prefectures, to lead their followers to execute Chuo Ji; Chuo Ji feared this, and his clan submitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Qu Yu, head of the sixteen affiliated Qiang prefectures, and Luo Ya of twelve prefectures to put Chuo Ji to death; Chuo Ji, afraid, brought his clan over in submission.

sentences.zh: 以屈遇爲檢校太保、歸德將軍，羅崖、啜佶並爲檢校司徒、懷化將軍。

translations.literal: Qu Yu was made Acting Grand Mentor and General Who Pacifies Virtue; Luo Ya and Chuo Ji were both made Acting Minister of Education and Generals Who Cherish Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yu was appointed Acting Grand Mentor and General Who Pacifies Virtue; Luo Ya and Chuo Ji were both made Acting Minister of Education and Generals Who Cherish Transformation.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年二月，靈州部送歲市官馬，賂所過族帳物粗惡，羌人恚不受。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Taiping Xingguo, when Lingzhou escorted the yearly official horse market, the gifts to tribal encampments along the way were coarse and inferior, and the Qiang, incensed, refused to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Taiping Xingguo 2, escorts from Lingzhou bringing the annual official horse market gave tribal encampments along the route shoddy gifts; the Qiang refused them in anger.

sentences.zh: 知州、比部郎中張全操捕得十八人殺之，沒入其兵仗羊馬，戎人遂擾。

translations.literal: The prefect and Bibu Langzhong Zhang Quancao captured eighteen men and killed them, confiscated their weapons, sheep, and horses, and the frontier peoples then rose in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Quancao, a director in the Ministry of Revenue, seized eighteen men and executed them, confiscated their arms and livestock, and the border peoples soon turned restive.

sentences.zh: 上遣使齎金帛撫賜其族，與之盟，始定。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys bearing gold and silks to soothe and grant gifts to their tribes, made a covenant with them, and order was finally restored.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys with gold and silk to soothe the tribes, renewed the covenant, and peace was restored.

sentences.zh: 召全操下有司鞫之，決杖流登州沙門島。

translations.literal: Zhang Quancao was summoned and interrogated by the relevant offices; he was sentenced to cane blows and exile to Shamen Island in Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quancao was summoned for trial; he was caned and exiled to Shamen Island off Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是歲，靈州通遠軍界嗓咩族、折四族、吐蕃村族、柰㖞三家族、尾落族、柰家族、嗓泥族剽略官綱，詔靈州安守忠、通遠軍董遵誨討平之。

translations.literal: That year, within the jurisdiction of Tongyuan Army in Lingzhou, the Sangmie, Zhesi, Tubo Village, Nai'e Sanjia, Weiluo, Nai, and Sangni clans plundered official transport; an edict ordered An Shouzhong of Lingzhou and Dong Zunhui of Tongyuan Army to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Sangmie, Zhesi, Tubo Village, Nai'e Sanjia, Weiluo, Nai, and Sangni clans on Lingzhou's Tongyuan Army frontier plundered official convoys; An Shouzhong of Lingzhou and Dong Zunhui of Tongyuan were ordered to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 六年，府州外浪族首領來都等來貢馬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Lai Dou, chieftain of the Wailang clan in Fuzhou, came to present horses in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 6 Lai Dou, chieftain of the Wailang clan at Fu Prefecture, presented horses in tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年，豐州大首領黃羅並弟乞蚌等來貢馬。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Huang Luo, great chieftain of Fengzhou, and his younger brother Qi Bang and others came to present horses in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 7 Huang Luo, a chief of Feng Prefecture, and his younger brother Qi Bang and others brought horses in tribute.

sentences.zh: 又銀州羌部拓跋遇來訴本州賦役苛虐，乞移居內地，詔令各守族帳。

translations.literal: Also, Tubo Yu of the Qiang in Yinzhou came to complain that this prefecture's levies and corvée were harsh and oppressive, begging to move into the interior; an edict ordered each to remain at his tribal encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo Yu of Yin Prefecture's Qiang also petitioned that local levies were oppressive and asked to move inland; the court ordered the tribes to remain at their encampments.

sentences.zh: 又保細族結集扇動諸部，夏州巡檢使梁迥率兵討平之。

translations.literal: Also, the Baoxi clan gathered and incited the various tribes; Liang Jiong, Xiujian envoy of Xiazhou, led troops to suppress and pacify them.
